title: Grove ships integration code it is not yet safe to use and disables it by mandating a rate limit of zero
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.13.1.2 states the mandate plainly: "Note that this function was deployed **without integration testing**, so its rate limit must be kept at `0` until the LayerZero dependencies are live and the functionality has been thoroughly integration tested."

This reveals a second role for the rate-limit system. Because every metered function calls `_rateLimited(key, amount)` before acting, a limit of zero makes the function unconditionally revert for any non-zero amount. The limit registry therefore doubles as a **per-function enable flag** that governance controls without redeploying code.

The same chunk shows two neighbouring cases of the same discipline. A...13.1.3 warns that the `approvalRequired == false` branch cannot be integration tested "without OFTs with `approvalRequired == false`" and must be tested before production use. A...11.1.7 warns that `redeemPendlePT` "must not be used for markets with non-standard SYs (such as ePENDLE, mPENDLE, or aTokens like aUSDC and aUSDT) without additional testing targeting each such market."

The trade-off is honest but real. Shipping dormant code keeps deployment cadence decoupled from integration readiness, and the zero limit is a strong technical guarantee — but the safety now depends on a *configuration value* rather than on the code's absence, so any process that sets limits in bulk, or any future refactor that stops routing through `_rateLimited`, silently arms the untested path.
description: The Atlas requires LIMIT_LAYERZERO_TRANSFER to stay at 0 until the dependency is live and integration tested, making the rate limit a governance kill switch rather than only a throttle.
